title: The Songhay empire
hookLine: Askia Muhammad's empire and his Hajj

cards: A ruler holds a huge stretch of the Niger valley: armies, towns, river fleets, taxes coming in. And what does he do? He sits down and writes questions to a scholar.
How should a Muslim ruler treat people who pray but still keep the old idols? What do I do about judges who take bribes? When is it right to take someone's property, and when is it theft?
The scholar, al-Maghili, wrote back, and his answers were kept. The ruler was Askia Muhammad. Today: the Songhay empire.

teach.b: Songhay grew up along the Niger, the river people of Gao, and in time its rulers took over towns that had once looked to Mali: Timbuktu, Djenné, the markets of the river bend.
The chronicles of Timbuktu, the Ta'rikh al-Sudan and the Ta'rikh al-Fattash, tell the story from the scholars' side.
One ruler, Sunni Ali, was a great conqueror, and the chronicles remember him harshly, as a man who mistreated the scholars of Timbuktu.
After his death, one of his commanders, Muhammad, took power and became the askia, the title of the new line of kings. The chronicles remember him very differently.
He kept scholars close, appointed judges, and asked questions. And he made the Hajj. The Qur'an pictures pilgrims arriving from everywhere.
In Pickthall's translation: "They will come unto thee on foot and on every lean camel; they will come from every deep ravine." Askia Muhammad came from very far.

teach.h: NAMED A DEPUTY ON THE JOURNEY.
teach.b: The chronicles say he gave generously in the holy cities, and that on this journey he was named a khalifa, a deputy, over the lands of West Africa, though they differ on who named him.
He came home with a title that tied his rule to something larger than his own armies. His story asks a quiet question: what makes power legitimate?
For him, part of the answer was going a long way to stand among other pilgrims, and part was being willing to ask a scholar how to rule well.

how: Historians and Muslims in the Sahel read the Timbuktu chronicles and al-Maghili's replies to Askia Muhammad to understand how Songhay's rulers and scholars worked together.

games.q: you've just taken power over a river empire. your judges take bribes and your people mix old ways with new. what do you do first?
o: replace everyone with your own soldiers.
write to a scholar and ask how a just ruler should act.
leave things alone and keep the peace.
games.why: Askia Muhammad wrote to al-Maghili with questions like these, and the scholar's replies were kept.

practice: A pilgrimage is a journey made not for business or holiday but to stand somewhere that matters: some Muslims long for Hajj for years, others make smaller journeys, to a grave, a mosque, a teacher.

Let a place your feet have taken you for a reason like that, or a place you hope they will, come to mind, and stay with it. If you pray, ask God for the way to get there; if not, simply hold the place in mind.

wordCard.voice: Khalifa. A deputy or successor, the title Askia Muhammad of the Songhay empire was given on his Hajj. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: a deputy or successor. The chronicles say Askia Muhammad was named one on his Hajj.

carryVoice: Your line: the askia. A ruler with armies, who still wrote down his questions. See you tomorrow.
